title: Cytron Maker Pi RP2040 Board Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A hover-to-explore overlay on the Cytron Maker Pi RP2040 pinout diagram. Every connector, button, LED, and chip on the board has a hotspot; hovering it describes the part, its GPIO pins, and a practical tip below the drawing. A quiz asks students to find each part by its job.

educational.topic: Parts of the Cytron Maker Pi RP2040 robot controller board and their GPIO pins
learningObjectives: Explain what each part of the Cytron Maker Pi RP2040 board does in a robot.
Identify the GPIO pins used by the motors, servos, buzzer, RGB LEDs, buttons, and Grove ports.
Explain the roles of the RP2040 microcontroller, the crystal, and the Boot and Reset buttons.
Use the motor status LEDs, motor test buttons, and GPIO status LEDs as debugging tools.
prerequisites: GPIO pins and config.py pin names

technical.framework: Custom JavaScript (shared hover-overlay engine on a static image)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Hover-to-explore labeled diagram followed by function-based retrieval practice
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Students hover (or tap) any part of the board or its printed label to see its job, GPIO pins, and a tip below the drawing; multi-part groups such as the Grove ports light up together with a tag naming the exact instance. Quiz mode asks students to click the part that answers a job-based question and scores first-try answers.
keyQuestions: Which parts let you test the motors before writing any code?
Which Grove port matches the I2C pins in your kit's config.py?
What is the difference between the Reset button and the Boot button?
Why can a GPIO pin not drive a motor directly?
commonMisconceptions: The GPIO pins can power a motor directly without the motor driver.
You must press the Boot button every time you upload a program from Thonny.
The Maker Pi RP2040 has WiFi because it uses a Raspberry Pi chip.
The mute switch stops the program that plays sounds.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz Me mode: find ten parts by their job and track the first-try score.
Exit ticket: list three parts to check, in order, when the wheels don't move.
Find the two unlabeled parts (RP2040 and crystal) and explain why a robot needs each.
